summary.title: The 4 biggest problems with homemade billing systems
summary.one_liner: Homemade SaaS billing engines tend to become a costly, never-ending project, and this Lago article draws on Qonto's experience to explain why.
keywords: why not build your own billing
takeaways: Building billing in-house often starts as a small project but grows into a full-time job for one or more engineers.
Changes such as yearly plans, switching from anniversary to calendar billing dates, new countries, and tax changes each required major rework at Qonto.
Grandfathered customers on old plans force teams to maintain legacy billing logic alongside new rules.
Processing high event volumes and generating millions of invoices accurately is hard, and fixes can require reprocessing without double-ingesting events.
The author recommends deciding on build vs buy early, since off-the-shelf tools may be inflexible and switching later is costly.
summary.summary: This Lago blog post, written by Vincent Pochet, a former backend engineer at Qonto, describes his experience building an internal billing system for a B2B neobank. It walks through concrete incidents such as adding a yearly plan, a forced migration of 100,000 customers from anniversary to calendar billing dates, and the difficulty of scaling event processing and invoice generation. It also cites Algolia's billing rebuilds as a parallel, and argues that billing is a living system that needs ongoing maintenance. The conclusion is a strong recommendation against building billing yourself.
